items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the
location of environmental facilities
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1031

SPONSOR: STEWART-COUSINS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the
location of environmental facilities

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the bill is to make provision regarding equitable siting
of environmental facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill sets forth the legislative intent of addressing
the issue of environmental equity.

Section 2 of the bill amends Section 1-0303 of the Environmental Conser-
vation law by adding three new subdivisions to define:  Economically
distressed area; Minority community; and Ethnic group.

Section 3 of the bill amends subdivision 2 of Section 8-0109 of the
Environmental Conservation Law by adding a new paragraph (h-1) to
require the Department of Environmental Conservation to modify its
permitting, monitoring and enforcement standards to address high concen-
trations of environmental facilities in racial minority and economically
distressed communities.

Sections 4 and 5 require all agencies and applicants who plan to
construct and/or manage environmental facilities in racial minority and
economically distressed communities to submit an economic development
plan, to determine whether such action may cause or increase a
disproportionate and/or inequitable burden on those minority communities
and/or economically distressed areas that are directly or significantly
indirectly affected by the action.

Section 6 of the bill is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

There has been an inequitable pattern in the siting of environmental
facilities in minority and economically distressed communities, which
have borne a disproportionate and inequitable share of such facilities.
This bill would require the state to factor in disproportionate or ineq-
uitable burdens on minority communities or economically distressed areas
under the State Environmental Quality Review Act.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill - 2012 - S6689 - Died Environmental Conservation
2013-14 - S692 - Died - Environmental Conservation
2015-16 - S3205 - Died - Environmental Conservation
2017 - 18 - S2953 - Died - Environmental Conservation
2019-20 - S5540 - Died - Environmental Conservation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after it shall have become
law; provided that section three of this act shall not apply to any
person who has received an initial determination pursuant to subdivision
4 of section 8-0109 of the environmental conservation law prior to such
date and provided further that section five of this act shall not apply
to any determination of significance made prior to such date.

AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1031C

SPONSOR: STEWART-COUSINS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the
location of environmental facilities

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the bill is to make provision regarding equitable siting
of environmental facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill sets forth the legislative intent of addressing
the issue of environmental equity.

Section 2 of the bill amends Section 8-0105 of the Environmental Conser-
vation Law by adding six new subdivisions defining "environmental
justice community," "economically distressed area," "ethnic group,"
"disadvantaged community," "minority community" and "existing burden
report."

Section 3 of the bill amends subdivision 2 of Section 8-0109 of the
Environmental Conservation Law by amending paragraph (h) to require
consideration of the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act and
adding a new paragraph (k) requiring that an environmental impact state-
ment consider effects of any proposed action on environmental justice
communities or disadvantaged communities, including whether the action
may cause or contribute to, either directly or indirectly, a dispropor-
tionate or inequitable pollution burden on those communities.

Section 4 of the bill amends subdivision 4 of Section 8-0109 of the
Environmental Conservation Law by requiring applicants for major
projects that may affect an environmental justice or disadvantaged
community to prepare and existing burden report prior to a determination
as to whether an environmental impact statement must be prepared for the
project.

Section 5 of the bill amends subdivision 8 of Section 8-0109 of the
Environmental Conservation Law to provide that no action shall be
carried out or approved if it may cause or contribute to, either direct-
ly or indirectly, a disproportionate or inequitable pollution burden on
an environmental justice or disadvantaged community, and adds a new
subdivision 10 providing that construction or expansion of certain
facilities in an environmental justice or disadvantaged community will
require preparation of an existing burden report.

Section 6 of the bill amends subparagraph (i) of paragraph (c) of subdi-
vision 2 of Section 8-0113 of the Environmental Conservation Law to
require the Department of Environmental Conservation to promulgate
implementing regulations.

Section 7 of the bill amends subdivision 2 of Section 8-0113 of the
Environmental Conservation Law by adding a new paragraph (m) specifying
the required contents of an existing burden report.

Section 8 of the bill is the effective date.
 
JUSTIFICATION:

There has been an inequitable pattern in the siting of polluting facili-
ties in environmental justice and disadvantaged communities, which have
borne a disproportionate and inequitable pollution burden from such
facilities. This bill requires state and local agencies to consider
potential disproportionate or inequitable pollution impacts on environ-
mental justice and disadvantaged communities as part of the environ-
mental review of such projects.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill - 2012 - S6689 - Died Environmental Conservation

2013-14 - 5692 - Died - Environmental Conservation

2015-16 - 53205 - Died - Environmental Conservation

2017-18 - 52953 - Died - Environmental Conservation

2019-20 - 55540 - Died - Environmental Conservation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after it shall have become
law; provided that section three of this act shall not apply to any
person who has received an initial determination pursuant to subdivision
4 of section 8-0109 of the environmental conservation law prior to such
date and provided further that section six of this act shall not apply
to any determination of significance made prior to such date.

summary: Makes various provisions regulating the location of environmental facilities to insure equity of treatment for minority communities or economically distressed areas or disadvantaged communities; requires environmental impact statements to state whether the siting of a facility will cause or increase a disproportionate burden on such areas.
title: Makes provisions regarding the siting of environmental facilities in minority communities, economically distressed areas or disadvantaged communities
